title_vi: Vì sao Redis nhanh như vậy?

source_snapshot.note: Fetched the pinned commit from GitHub; git rev-parse of the path gives the source map's blob OID. Non-empty source body read; no source-image bytes used.

related.reason_vi: Dữ liệu trong bộ nhớ nhanh nhưng cần cách ghi xuống đĩa để không mất.
Các con số độ trễ của bộ nhớ, mạng và đĩa.
Luồng I/O của 6.0 trong quá trình phát triển kiến trúc Redis.

claims.evidence: Statements were checked against the Redis latency, FAQ and memory optimization pages of redis/docs at commit 3b030c7ef066c0bb7f88ddec02c784e49783b0f8 and the Redis 7.0.15 source (src/ae.c, redis.conf), read from partial clones; numbers come from an experiment run on 2026-10-18 with the Ubuntu redis-server 7.0.15 package on a 4-core Linux container.

mobile.evidence: Chromium (Playwright 1.56, headless) rendered lesson.md converted by markdown-it (CommonMark, tables, raw HTML) with a 16 px page gutter and every <details> open, at 320, 375 and 430 px: document scrollWidth equalled the viewport at each width. Smallest figure text from the SVG font sizes times the shown scale: 13.5 px at 320, 15.0 px at 375. python3 -m scripts.figures check --browser measured every figure line. Not GitHub's renderer, not a real phone, not learner testing.

claims.claim_vi: Redis is mostly single threaded: one process serves all requests with multiplexing, one request at a time; it is fast mainly because it does not block on system calls and normal commands take very little time; a slow command makes all other clients wait; KEYS is a common source of latency; threads since 2.4 do some slow disk I/O in the background.
claims.section: Single threaded nature of Redis; Latency generated by slow commands
claims.verified_by: Read; the experiment measured KEYS * on 2,000,000 keys at 1,574,062 microseconds in SLOWLOG and a PING sent during it waited 1538 ms.

claims.claim_vi: To use several cores, run several Redis instances or shard; since 4.0 some actions such as background deletion are threaded.
claims.section: How can Redis use multiple CPUs or cores?
claims.verified_by: Read from a partial clone of redis/docs.

claims.claim_vi: Small hashes, lists, sets and sorted sets use a special compact encoding up to configurable limits (hash-max-listpack-entries 512, set-max-intset-entries 512).
claims.section: Special encoding of small aggregate data types; ADVANCED CONFIG
claims.verified_by: Read; the experiment showed a 512-field hash as listpack using 6192 bytes and a 513-field hash as hashtable using 28816 bytes (MEMORY USAGE), a three-integer set as intset.

claims.claim_vi: The event loop includes the best multiplexing layer available: evport, then epoll, then kqueue, then select.
Client socket reads and writes can be handled by I/O threads (io-threads), disabled by default and advised only on machines with at least 4 cores when Redis is CPU-bound.
claims.verified_by: Read the 7.0.15 redis.conf; CONFIG GET io-threads returned 1 in the experiment.

claims.claim_vi: Experiment: with 50 clients redis-benchmark gave about 66 thousand SET per second without pipelining and about 593 thousand with 16 commands per round trip (GET about 73 thousand and 683 thousand).
claims.verified_by: Own measurement on one machine over loopback; the URL is the configuration of the version measured. Not a general figure.

design_notes_vi: Ba thẻ lý do có biểu tượng, ba ghi chú đo. Không ghi con số so bộ nhớ với đĩa vì chưa đo. Vẽ bằng scripts/figures.
source_deviations: Source states that RAM access is at least 1000 times faster than random disk access; the lesson does not repeat a figure it did not measure or source.
Source lists the three reasons without their cost; the lesson adds that single-threaded execution makes one slow command block every client, with a measurement.
Source mentions efficient lower-level data structures without naming them; the lesson shows listpack and intset and the size jump past the 512-entry threshold.
